body:
Should this be `std`?
```suggestion
use std::future::Future;
```

Doesn't `async` already have semantics that would make a suitable as a replacement to `Lazy` here? IIRC `async` functions don't get executed until they get polled. Or does `.await` imply taking ownership?
I'd prefer a default timeout closer to the current command timeout of 500ms.
I've set it to 700, lmk if that sounds ok.
Would you please use `async-process` for async commands for now? I think it would be better to avoid as many unstable features as possible.

body: If you want to get this changed I would prefer you do this in a separate PR.

`utils::exec_cmd` has (mostly) moved into `Context` and I don't think that would work this kind of design (I'd prefer it remain there, even once this pr is merged for better command mocking and caching in the future). It looks like `futures` provides `shared` which would allow resolving a future multiple times, but I wasn't able to figure out how to resolve the ownership problems around that.

I've just seen that utils/Context PR merge, indeed, it's going to need some reworking.

So you're saying it's ok to depend on `futures`, in addition to `async_std`, correct? I had actually tried to avoid adding it in the first pass :smile:
Adding it should be fine, but I don't have much experience with async in rust. I didn't really notice much of an impact on compile times, is there any other reason to avoid it?
I'm also not seeing increased compile times. The idea was just to keep dependencies focused, but otherwise there shouldn't be any issues. It will actually improve some areas.

body: Moved to https://github.com/starship/starship/pull/2299

The issue with switching rust to use `Context` is that `context::exec_cmd` will return `None` when the subprocess exits with error, but this seems like an acceptable case for `rustup`. Prefer adding another method to `Context` to also report exit status, or employing `time_limit` manually here?

I think `exec_cmd` already handles errors sufficiently by logging them. If you think the real error is required here, I'd prefer you add a second method to `Context`.
Beyond that: I think for modules that are async it makes sense to ignore `command_timeout` because having multiple separate timeouts for a single module would get confusing.
